races.title: State Assembly, District 37
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Gregg Hart
cands.bio: Democratic member of the California State Assembly for District 37 since December 2022. Previously served on the Santa Barbara County Board of Supervisors (elected 2018) and four terms on the Santa Barbara City Council. Former legislative assistant to an Assemblymember, SBCAG Traffic Solutions manager, and preschool owner.

endorsements.text: California Federation of Labor Unions, AFL-CIO

cands.gaps: We could not find where Hart was born or raised, or when he came to California. We found no documented actions or stated positions from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, growth limits, immigration and H-1B, police pay, gun laws, abortion or school choice. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2022, 2024 or 2026. We found no public statements from him on data centers or development, and no controversies, foreign ties or notable stories about him in the pages we had.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Assembly member since 2022; Santa Barbara County Supervisor from 2018; four terms on the Santa Barbara City Council; legislative assistant to Assemblymember Jack O'Connell; SBCAG Traffic Solutions manager and later deputy executive director; owned a preschool for 20 years.
qual.why: He has prior and current legislative service, local elected office, legislative staff experience and public-agency management, plus running a small business. Committee seats were not counted.

cands.name: Sari Domingues
cands.bio: Retired government business analyst with a 30-year public-sector career at the Santa Maria-Bonita School District, Santa Barbara County and Monterey County. Republican candidate for Assembly District 37 in 2024 and 2026. Has held no elected office. Affiliated with Moms for Liberty Santa Barbara County.

endorsements.text: Republican Party of California (listed for 2024 and 2026), Reform California (2026), and several conservative voter guides in 2026.
In her 2024 survey she listed the Santa Barbara Republican Central Committee and the San Luis Obispo Republican Central Committee as endorsers.

cands.gaps: She has never held elected office, so there are no votes or official actions to report. We found no documented positions from her on data centers, development or land use, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor ownership of land, H-1B or immigration enforcement, gun policy, abortion, or teacher pay. She did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey, and the only survey answers available are from 2024. Her campaign site's "Parents Choice" banner and her stated aim to "push for primary education" and parent rights do not spell out a school-choice or voucher position, so we did not count them. We could not independently verify her upbringing or career beyond Ballotpedia and her own campaign site. We found no news coverage of controversies.

local.label: Roots 100: Ballotpedia says she was born in Santa Maria, and her campaign site says she was born and raised there, attending St. Mary's school and Santa Maria High School.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Her campaign site says she spent 30 years in government service, at the Santa Maria-Bonita School District, Santa Barbara County and Monterey County, retiring as a Business Analyst supporting HR, payroll, benefits, retirement and financial ERP systems for a workforce of over 5,000. She has no elected or legislative experience.
qual.why: The career is long public-sector analyst and systems work, which is a middle-range background. She has held no elected office and has no legislative, law or budget-writing record, so she scores in the middle band, not the high one.
